header: The rules of a password's life (pure, no database, no clock of its own: every function is given the time it needs):
- a new password is valid for 180 DAYS; after that the person is taken to the change window as soon as he has signed in, with the number of days said in the message;
- the last 5 passwords cannot be used again;

- a person with no recorded change (every account before this rule, still on its first password) is not shut out on the day the rule starts: his 180 days begin at his first sign-in after it, and are then recorded;
- the OTP (a one-time code to the person's own phone or e-mail before a password is changed) is built but SWITCHED OFF until PASSWORD_OTP=on on the host.
I keep the messages here, once, so the window and the server say the same words.

symbols.name: HISTORY_KEEP
doc: Sets how many earlier passwords cannot be used again

symbols.name: REUSED_MESSAGE
symbols.sig: const REUSED_MESSAGE = `You cannot use any of your last ${HISTORY_KEEP} passwords again. Please choose one you have not used recently.`

symbols.name: SAME_AS_CURRENT_MESSAGE
symbols.sig: const SAME_AS_CURRENT_MESSAGE = "The new password cannot be the same as your current (last) password."

symbols.name: Age
symbols.sig: | { state: "unrecorded" } | { state: "valid"; daysLeft: number; expiresAt: number } | { state: "expired"; daysOver: number; expiresAt: number }
doc: All times here are epoch milliseconds. I keep dates in Luxon in this program: src/lib/dates.selftest.ts forbids the built-in Date.

symbols.name: ageStatus
symbols.sig: export function ageStatus(changedAt: number | null | undefined, now: number, validDays: number = PASSWORD_VALID_DAYS): Age
doc: Says where a password stands: never recorded, still valid (with the days left, counted up: the last day is 1), or expired

symbols.name: OtpConfig
doc: ---- the one-time code (OTP): switched off until the host says on ----

members.name: on
doc: The master switch: PASSWORD_OTP=on (also 1, true, yes). I treat anything else as off.

members.name: noChannel
doc: What to do with a person who has no mobile number and no e-mail on record: I let him change with the current password alone (allow, the default: otherwise the 180-day rule would shut him out) or refuse (block)

symbols.name: otpConfig
symbols.sig: export function otpConfig(env: { PASSWORD_OTP?: string; PASSWORD_OTP_NO_CHANNEL?: string }): OtpConfig

doc: I let the screen say only this about the destination: "XXXXXX1234", "a•••@sail.in"
